record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: A group G is called strictly bounded if for m some positive integer n, each of its subgroups of the form hxy | m ∈ Zi (x, y ∈ G) has a generating set of size n. Does every strictly bounded right-orderable group have a Conrad right order?

evidence.quote: 2.7. (A. H. Rhemtulla [81]) A group G is called strictly bounded if for m some positive integer n, each of its subgroups of the form hxy | m ∈ Zi (x, y ∈ G) has a generating set of size n. Does every strictly bounded right-orderable group have a Conrad right order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A right order on a group $G$ is a total order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a\le b$ implies $ac\le bc$ for all $a,b,c\in G$. A right order $\le$ on $G$ is called a Conrad right order (or is said to satisfy the Conrad property) if for all positive elements $a,b\in G$ (i.e. $a,b>1$), there exists a positive integer $N$ such that $a^N b > a$.

A group $G$ is called strictly bounded if there exists a positive integer $n$ such that for every pair of elements $x,y\in G$, the subgroup $\langle x^m y \mid m\in\mathbb{Z}\rangle$ admits a generating set of size at most $n$.

Question: Does every strictly bounded right-orderable group admit a Conrad right order?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an unsolved problem in the theory of ordered and orderable groups, attributed to A. H. Rhemtulla. Related questions about Conrad right orders on right-orderable groups (e.g., for n-Engel groups, or for groups with no nonabelian free subsemigroups) appear in surveys and recent literature, but no resolution of this specific question for strictly bounded right-orderable groups was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Conradian/Conrad right orders on right-orderable groups.
status_evidence.claim: Conrad property and related questions remain active topics; the strictly bounded case is not reported as resolved.
